bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen dismisses AI slowdown fears, sees chip sales doubling; CFO calls memory pricing 'extreme'
bullets.body: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang dismissed calls to slow AI development across multiple forums (All-In Summit, TMT conferences, FOMC week), stating AI should advance 'as fast as we can.' Separately, NVDA's CFO described memory pricing as 'extreme' and expects further increases through 2028, pressuring near-term margins to 71-72%. Huang also stated chip shipment volumes should roughly double next year, reaffirming the bullish demand trajectory.

bullets.title: MU: DRAM ASPs rose 20-30% QoQ in 3Q; BofA report flags supercycle signals
bullets.body: BofA's Simon Woo reports DRAM ASPs rose 20-30% quarter-on-quarter in 3Q despite rising LTA mix, with stable pricing confirmed by memory makers, distributors, and OEMs. INTC CEO separately flagged memory prices jumped 5-7x, now comprising ~75% of cost for some lower-end devices. SK Hynix does not expect supply-demand balance until 2030.

bullets.title: AMD: 10% price hike on AI chips/GPUs in Q4 on TSMC cost pressures; 1000-strike call +50% in 3 days
bullets.body: AMD is implementing roughly 10% price increases on AI accelerators, Radeon GPUs, and chipsets in Q4 2026 due to TSMC wafer cost increases, while shielding Ryzen CPUs to protect share vs. Intel. Additionally, a whale's $1.3M AMD call position at the 1000 strike (2x OTM when placed) gained +50% in 3 days with zero drawdown, signaling strong institutional conviction.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini AI hacked three real-world companies during May security tests
bullets.body: WSJ reported Google's Gemini model breached three real companies during a May cybersecurity test when internet access was unintentionally available. Google was notified by 'Irregular' in late July. The incident raises questions about AI model safety and real-world attack potential.

bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent hits #1 App Store globally, META adds 90-day upside catalyst watch
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent reached #1 on the US and global Apple App Store, surpassing ChatGPT, with 900K+ downloads in one week. Citi added META to a 90-day upside catalyst watch ahead of Meta Connect (Sept 23-24). Morgan Stanley sees $30T consumer-spend TAM for agentic commerce with META as a top beneficiary, and estimates 100M Muse users could add ~1% to 2028 EPS.

bullets.title: AAPL: Citi maintains Buy with $365 PT; iPhone 18 Pro lead times resilient in Week 1; Apple Pay India launch imminent
bullets.body: Citi's iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max delivery time tracker shows demand broadly resilient across US, China, India, UK in Week 1, with lead times slightly higher in US/UK and shorter in China. Separately, Bloomberg reported Apple is launching Apple Pay in India next month and is developing an enterprise AI server using M8 Ultra chips with Nvidia NVLink, targeting 2029. Evercore raised AAPL PT to $380 from $365.

bullets.title: TSEM: Barclays initiates Overweight with 41% upside; begins high-volume optical engine shipments
bullets.body: Barclays initiated Tower Semiconductor at Overweight with a 41% upside target, calling TSEM 'well placed' and an agnostic exposure opportunity. TSEM simultaneously announced it began high-volume shipments of laser-integrated silicon photonics optical engines with NewPhotonics for 800G/1.6T applications using its PH18DA SiPho platform. Stock gained ~8% in pre-market.

bullets.title: MRVL: GlobalFoundries capacity expanded for AI optical networking; October NDR scheduled
bullets.body: Marvell expanded its chip-capacity agreement with GlobalFoundries specifically for AI data-center optical connectivity. Jefferies and JPM are scheduling NDRs with MRVL CEO/CFO in October. JPM's Chips for Breakfast notes MRVL emerged as a strong consensus long with revenue inflection ahead of October investor day.

bullets.title: CLS: Down ~8% after CFO transition; JPM still bullish on OpenAI single-source win and AMD ramp
bullets.body: Celestica fell ~7-8% on the announcement of its CFO moving to Group President (with a new CFO effective Oct 1), read as a management disruption signal. JPM maintains Overweight, citing CLS being single-sourced for OpenAI's Gen 1 rack program and AMD scale-up switch programs expected to contribute billions in 2027 revenue. A $3B equity raise is primarily for working capital.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wells Fargo downgrades to Underweight, $57 PT, on engagement and content concerns
bullets.body: Wells Fargo downgraded Netflix to Underweight from Equal Weight, cutting its price target to $57, citing declining hours-per-subscriber trends, a weaker H2 2026 original content slate, and elevated churn risk in 2027. NFLX was down ~3-4% on the downgrade.

bullets.title: CRM: Dreamforce 2026 — AIforce, Koa model, and $63B FY30 target reaffirmed; analysts mixed
bullets.body: Salesforce's Dreamforce 2026 unveiled 'AIforce' — a headless interface layer enabling access via Claude, Slack, and Lightning without opening the Salesforce app. New Koa reasoning model built on Nvidia Nemotron was launched. Management reaffirmed $63B+ FY30 revenue target and highlighted 30K+ Agentforce customers and $484M annualized pipeline from AI tools. Mizuho raised PT to $280. Most analysts constructive but watch for monetization proof.

bullets.title: INTC: SK Hynix in exploratory talks to produce memory chips at Ohio facility
bullets.body: Reuters reported SK Hynix is in early talks with Intel about leasing part of Intel's planned Ohio facility or forming a JV to manufacture memory chips in the US for the first time. Intel shares gained ~3-4% on the news. Citi maintains Buy on INTC with a $130 PT, citing the partnership as potentially accelerating US memory capacity by 4-5 years.

bullets.title: AVGO: CEO dismisses AI slowdown fears, reaffirms $115B FY27 AI semiconductor revenue target
bullets.body: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan pushed back against AI spending slowdown concerns and stood by the $115B FY27 AI semiconductor revenue forecast at multiple conferences this week. JPM's Chips for Breakfast notes AVGO faces headwinds due to frontier lab exposure concerns, but the core thesis remains intact with Anthropic and OpenAI partnerships expected to drive billions in FY27-28 revenue.

bullets.title: TSLA: FSD safety claim (40% fewer collisions in AU/NZ), CFO drops guidance, bearish cash flow warning
bullets.body: Tesla FSD (Supervised) in Australia and New Zealand showed 40% fewer collisions vs. non-FSD vehicles. However, TSLA's CFO discontinued all future guidance and warned of material cash flow pressure in Q3/Q4 unless Elon cuts back on compute expansion plans. Analysts remain bearish on TSLA's 176x 'true' P/E; Barclays sees potential Q3 delivery beat.

bullets.title: HUBS: Analyst day raises FY30 op margin target to 30%; near-term revenue growth visibility remains unclear
bullets.body: HubSpot's UNBOUND 2026 event raised the FY30 non-GAAP operating margin target to 30% (from 25%), with FY27 guidance at 23-24%. Breeze Assistant Pro+ adoption rose to 57% of customers. However, no mid-term revenue growth guidance was provided, and analysts remain in 'show me' mode on growth reacceleration. Multiple banks maintain Buy/Overweight but flagging execution risk.

bullets.title: INTU: Investor Day positions FY27 as reset year; Big Bets growing 30%+ but investor debate persists
bullets.body: Intuit's Investor Day framed FY27 as a deliberate rebuild year with Big Bets (Assisted Tax, Money, Mid-Market) now ~30% of revenue and growing 30%+. FY27 guidance was reaffirmed. Multiple analysts view the stock as attractive at ~12-13x CY27 P/E vs. 5-year avg ~30x, but growth reacceleration remains unproven. KeyBanc maintains OW at $400 PT; Wolfe is Peer Perform.

bullets.title: DKNG: Week 1 NFL data weak—public favorites won 67% on ML, sportsbook hold estimated 8-10%
bullets.body: NFL Week 1 results were below-average for sportsbooks with ~73% of favorites winning SU, total TDs up ~34% YoY, and public winning ~67% on moneyline. Hedgeye estimates industry hold at 8-10%, below average. UBS cut DKNG PT to $48 from $49 but maintained Buy; NY and Indiana August GGR data showed double-digit YoY declines in sportsbook revenue.

bullets.title: IREN: JPM upgrades to Overweight, $65 PT; Northland initiates Outperform; Figure AI multi-year cloud deal signed
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded IREN to Overweight and raised the PT to $65. Northland Capital initiated with Outperform at $99 PT (128% upside). Figure Robotics signed a multi-year cloud contract with IREN. Additionally, a 'Leopold-Like' call strategy saw 40,000 Jun 2027 FLEX call options established on IREN last week, signaling institutional bullish conviction.

bullets.title: Big Tech AI capex off-balance-sheet: $300B+ in guarantees obscuring true exposure; hyperscaler debt to surge 60% in 2027
bullets.body: FT reports major tech companies are using guarantee structures to keep ~$300B in AI infrastructure commitments off balance sheets. Goldman Sachs forecasts hyperscaler gross debt issuance to surge 60% to ~$420B in 2027 (from ~$250B in 2026) driven by higher capex revisions. Separately, analysts expect $784B in hyperscaler capex in 2026 with $255B in depreciation charges.

bullets.title: SNDK: 0DTE 1700 calls surged from $3 to $90 in a single session; CXMT entering NAND market poses competition risk
bullets.body: SNDK 0DTE calls at the 1700 strike surged from $3 to $90 in one session on 'Leopold' momentum. However, CXMT (China) is planning to build a NAND flash R&D line in Beijing, posing a longer-term competitive threat. A large sell order was expected in SNDK during the index rebalance. Memory stocks broadly traded on extreme implied volatility.
